title: Fable agent audit: analyze plugin against Ongoing/Medusa WMS integration best practices
description:
## Why

The plugin has grown through many milestones (provider, workflows, subscribers, jobs, sync). We have never done a holistic, outside-in audit comparing our architecture and flows against (a) Ongoing Warehouse's own recommended integration patterns, (b) Medusa's official guidance on third-party/WMS integrations, and (c) how mature community Medusa fulfillment/IMS plugins structure the same concerns. This issue commissions that audit from a Fable-powered agent.

## What to do

Run this as a Fable model agent (claude-fable-5) with the `medusa-dev:building-with-medusa` skill loaded. The agent must:

1. **Read and understand the whole plugin** — src/providers, src/modules, src/workflows, src/subscribers, src/jobs, src/api, src/links, plus graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md (and graphify-out/wiki/index.md if present) for structure.

2. **Read and understand these required resources** (fetch them, don't rely on training data):
   - https://developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/webshop-flow — Ongoing's canonical webshop order flow
   - https://developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/inventory — inventory sync guidance
   - https://developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/paginating-responses
   - https://developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/parallel-requests — rate limiting/concurrency rules
   - https://developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/integrate-transport-system
   - https://developer.ongoingwarehouse.com/REST/v1/openapi.json?version=57 — API surface we should be using
   - https://github.com/Epic-Design-Labs/medusa-plugin-foundry-ims — comparable IMS plugin
   - https://github.com/pevey/medusa-plugins — community plugin patterns
   - https://github.com/medusajs/examples/tree/main/shipstation-integration — closest architectural model
   - https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/integrations/guides/shipstation
   - https://docs.medusajs.com/learn/best-practices/third-party-sync — Medusa's third-party sync best practices
   - https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/medusa-workflows-reference
   - https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/commerce-modules/fulfillment

3. **Research beyond the list**: search online for additional authoritative resources that should inform the audit — e.g. Ongoing developer docs pages not listed above (webhooks/automation triggers, article/order status models), Medusa docs on inventory module, event bus, scheduled jobs, workflow compensation/retry patterns, idempotency in integrations, and other production Medusa WMS/3PL integrations (e.g. other 3PL plugins on npm/GitHub). Incorporate what's relevant and cite it.

4. **Compare and analyze** across at least these dimensions:
   - Order push flow vs Ongoing's recommended webshop flow (statuses, when to send, cancellation/edit windows, idempotency)
   - Inventory sync direction/cadence vs Ongoing inventory guidance and Medusa third-party-sync best practices
   - Fulfillment provider contract completeness vs Medusa fulfillment module reference (options, validation, cancellation, returns, tracking)
   - Workflow design: compensation, retries, error propagation, long-running sync patterns
   - Rate limiting/pagination/parallel-request compliance with Ongoing's rules
   - Webhook vs polling strategy vs what Ongoing supports
   - Module isolation, links, and data-model choices vs Medusa conventions and the reference plugins
   - Gaps: features similar plugins have that we lack (or intentionally skip — note why if discernible)

## Deliverables

1. **A written report** committed nowhere — attach as the issue's notes or a linked markdown in the issue comments (`bd comments`), structured as: executive summary, per-dimension findings (what we do / what best practice says / verdict / evidence with links), and a prioritized recommendation list.
2. **Actionable beads issues filed** (`bd create`) for every concrete, worthwhile change the audit surfaces — each with type, priority, description referencing the report finding and the source resource, and dependencies between them where ordering matters. Link them to this issue (use this issue as parent or reference its ID in descriptions).
3. Purely informational findings (no action needed) stay in the report only.

## Acceptance criteria

- All 13 required resources above were actually fetched and reflected in the report (each cited at least once or explicitly marked not-applicable)
- At least one round of independent online research beyond the given list, with sources cited
- Report covers all 8 comparison dimensions
- Every actionable recommendation has a corresponding filed bead with priority and rationale
- Report attached to this issue via bd comments/notes
notes:
AUDIT COMPLETE. Report: docs/audits/2026-07-15-s1k-wms-integration-audit.md

EXEC SUMMARY: Medusa-side architecture is above reference quality (idempotent PUT-upsert push with deterministic order numbers persisted pre-PUT, sync-state ledger with classified errors + CAS-guarded retry/dead-letter, hybrid webhook+poll shipment detection, workflows for order-path mutations, clean module/link isolation). BUT the Ongoing HTTP client was never verified against the real REST spec — machine inspection of openapi.json v57 confirms: (C1/P0) pagination uses page/pageSize params that don't exist -> identical repeated requests, infinite loop when result >=50 rows (ji6); (C2/P0) GET /articles/inventory endpoint doesn't exist -> stock-sync 404s every tick (dtw); (C3/P1) tracking extraction reads parcels[].parcelTracking.code, real shape is parcels[].tracking.waybill -> poll-path tracking always empty (5vu). Also: throttle is per-client-instance so Ongoing's sequential-per-goods-owner rule isn't enforced process-wide (4s4); stockInfoChangedFrom delta sync unused (sw8); no article sync (sci); no wayOfDelivery mapping (rzd); N+1 inventory reconcile (3e8); webhook underused for status refresh (jzm); minor arch-workflow-required deviation in status-poll job (o6c); returns stubbed (9ah); stale graphify/CLAUDE.md (de5). All 13 required resources fetched + independent research cited in report. Filed 12 follow-up beads with deps ji6 <- dtw <- sw8.

title: order-updated.ts take:1 order_change query silently drops address/contact changes when bundled with other field edits
description:
Surfaced by whole-project Medusa-aware code review 2026-07-02 (CRIT-4, adversarially confirmed). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## File
`src/subscribers/order-updated.ts:44-73`

## Failure scenario

Admin edits `shipping_address` AND `locale` (or any address/contact field bundled with `metadata`/`locale`) in the same `updateOrderWorkflow` call. Medusa's `updateOrderWorkflow` (`node_modules/@medusajs/core-flows/dist/order/workflows/update-order.js:125-193`) builds a `changes` array pushing one object per changed field, then passes the whole array to `registerOrderChangesStep` → `OrderModuleService.registerOrderChange_` (`node_modules/@medusajs/order/dist/services/order-module-service.js:1223-1242`).

That module service does `orderChangeService_.create(inputData.map(...))` — **one order_change DB row per array entry**, each with a single-element `actions` array. All rows share the same `created_at` timestamp (or microsecond-close), and address types are always pushed earlier in the array than locale/metadata.

The subscriber's query `pagination: { take: 1, order: { created_at: 'DESC' } }` returns whichever row the DB picks — non-deterministic across the group. When the returned row is `locale`, `hasAddressContactChange` evaluates false → Ongoing is never re-synced for a real address change.

## Why the tests missed this

The unit test in `src/subscribers/__tests__/order-updated.test.ts:42-56` mocks all detail types on a single synthetic order_change row with multiple `actions`. That does not match the real one-row-per-change shape that `registerOrderChange_` produces.

## Recommended fix

Query all order_change rows for this `order_id`/`change_type` since the last processed watermark (or within the same instant as the newest row), union their detail types, and derive `changedTypes` from the union — not from a single row.

## Verification (from review)

Refute pass verified against actual Medusa v2.16.0 source under node_modules — confirmed one-row-per-change semantics; confirmed `order.updated` fires once per updateOrders call, not per field; confirmed the change_type filter does not narrow to one row per type.

title: cancelFulfillment silently succeeds when it decides Ongoing shouldn't cancel — Medusa marks fulfillment cancelled while Ongoing keeps shipping
description:
Surfaced by whole-project Medusa-aware code review 2026-07-02 (CRIT-3, adversarially confirmed). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## Files
- `src/providers/ongoing-fulfillment/service.ts:284` (main path)
- `src/providers/ongoing-fulfillment/service.ts:265` (no-identifier sub-case)

## Failure scenario

Order's Ongoing status has moved past the integration's `cancellable_status_codes`. `decideOngoingCancelStep` returns `{ shouldCancel: false, reason: 'status_not_cancellable' }`. Provider's `cancelFulfillment` returns `{ canceled: false, reason: 'status_not_cancellable' }` **without throwing**.

Medusa's core `FulfillmentModuleService.cancelFulfillment` (verified at `node_modules/@medusajs/fulfillment/dist/services/fulfillment-module-service.js:711-728`) only inspects throw/no-throw; on non-throw it unconditionally sets `fulfillment.canceled_at`. Result: Medusa shows the fulfillment as cancelled while Ongoing continues to pick, pack, and ship. The merchant believes the order was stopped; it wasn't.

Sub-case at line 265: when the fulfillment's stashed `data` lacks all three identifiers (`ongoing_order_number` / `medusa_fulfillment_id` / `medusa_order_id`), the provider also returns without throwing — same silent-mark-cancelled outcome even though no cancel request was ever sent.

## Plan-doc note

The plan for issue #22 lumped `status_not_cancellable` under "benign/idempotent" alongside `already_cancelled`. But those two have **opposite** real-world consequences: `already_cancelled` is a true no-op (Ongoing already stopped); `status_not_cancellable` isn't (Ongoing keeps shipping).

## Recommended fix

Throw a `MedusaError` (with a distinct type, e.g. `NOT_ALLOWED` or `INVALID_STATE`) for non-idempotent no-cancel outcomes so Medusa preserves the fulfillment's un-cancelled state. Only truly-idempotent successes (already cancelled) may resolve.

## Verification (from review)

Refute pass reviewed:
- Core Medusa module-service.js source: confirmed unconditional `canceled_at` set on any non-throw.
- The `order.canceled` subscriber independently re-runs `cancelOngoingOrderWorkflow`, but its ONGOING_EVENTS.ORDER_CANCELLED emit is gated on `shouldCancel === true`, so external event consumers aren't misled — but Medusa's own `fulfillment.canceled_at` field is wrong.
- No compensating mechanism found; no UI surfaces the mismatch.

title: putOrder returns { ongoingOrderId: undefined } when Ongoing's 2xx body omits orderId
description:
Surfaced by whole-project Medusa-aware code review 2026-07-02 (CRIT-2, adversarially confirmed). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## File
`src/lib/ongoing/client.ts:115`

## Failure scenario

Ongoing returns 2xx without `orderId` in the body (async-accepted, empty 200, unexpected shape). `res.orderId` is `undefined`, but the return type declares `ongoingOrderId: number`, so TypeScript lets it through.

Callers persist the undefined:
- `src/workflows/steps/push-order-record-sync.ts:54-55,100`
- `src/workflows/steps/upsert-ongoing-order-edit.ts:73-88`

Both assign `res.ongoingOrderId` straight into a variable persisted via `recordSync({..., ongoing_order_id: ongoingOrderId})` with no null/undefined check. All future cancel/status/tracking lookups for that order permanently fail with no error trail.

## Compare

`cancelOrder` already defensively does `res?.orderId ?? ongoingOrderId` — the pattern exists in the same file, applied inconsistently.

## Recommended fix

Add the same defensive fallback + explicit error throw when the field is missing, or run a lightweight runtime schema validation on the response. Prefer the throw path so a missing orderId is surfaced, not silently persisted.

## Note

Real-world probability depends on Ongoing's actual API contract (not verified in this review). The code gap is real and unmitigated regardless.

title: client.ts safeJson + unchecked cast lets malformed 2xx bodies flow into the domain
description:
Surfaced by whole-project Medusa-aware code review 2026-07-02 (CRIT-1, adversarially confirmed). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## Files
- `src/lib/ongoing/client.ts:71` (safeJson)
- `src/lib/ongoing/client.ts:84` (doFetch's `return parsed as T`)

## Failure scenario

Ongoing (or an intermediary proxy) returns HTTP 200 with a non-JSON body — HTML error page, truncated response, gateway timeout page. `safeJson` catches `JSON.parse`'s throw and returns the raw text string; `doFetch` casts the string to `T` with no content-type or shape validation. `putOrder` then reads `res.orderId` on a string, gets `undefined`, and returns `{ ongoingOrderId: undefined }` without ever surfacing an error. Downstream persistence writes an undefined into `OngoingOrderSync.ongoing_order_id` and every future cancel/tracking lookup permanently breaks with no error trail.

All other Ongoing operations flow through the same `doFetch` — this is the root of every downstream type-hole finding in the review.

## Recommended fix

- Validate `Content-Type: application/json` on the response before parsing.
- Throw a typed `OngoingApiError({ kind: 'terminal', reason: 'unexpected_body_shape' })` on mismatch.
- Do not swallow `JSON.parse` failures in `safeJson`.

## Verification (from review)

Verified by adversarial refute pass — confirmed no content-type or shape validation anywhere in `doFetch`; no test constructs a 200 response with malformed/non-JSON text; cancelOrder's `res?.orderId ?? ongoingOrderId` fallback is a symptom of the same gap, not a fix.

title: P3: Extract shared subscriber helper: persist-then-emit ordering and isolated event-bus try/catch
description:
Cross-shard epic from whole-project Medusa-aware code review 2026-07-02 (P3). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## Pattern

Two problems folded into one root cause across all three subscribers:

1. **Emit failures mis-labeled.** `eventBus.emit(...)` is called inside the same try/catch as the state-persisting workflow. If emit throws after the workflow already succeeded, the catch logs it as "workflow failed" — mis-attributing an event-bus outage to the workflow.

2. **Edit-blocked branches emit BEFORE persisting state.** In `order-updated.ts` and `order-edit-confirmed.ts`, the blocked branch calls `eventBus.emit(EDIT_BLOCKED, ...)` **before** `markOrderSyncEditBlockedWorkflow(...).run(...)`. If the emit throws, the state-persisting workflow is skipped entirely — the row's `edit_blocked_at`/`category`/`reason` never get written even though the blocking decision was correct.

## Instances (I10)

- `src/subscribers/order-updated.ts:140-148,194-202`
- `src/subscribers/order-edit-confirmed.ts:78-87`
- `src/subscribers/order-canceled.ts:76-84`

## Precedent

`src/jobs/stock-sync.ts:100-119` and `src/jobs/retry-failed-syncs.ts:90-105,140-153` already do this right: they wrap `eventBus.emit(...)` in its own try/catch with an explicit comment noting an event-bus outage must not surface as a "row/integration failed" log for work that actually succeeded. Persist first, emit in its own isolated try.

## Recommended fix

Extract a shared `processSyncRows(rows, handler, logger, eventLabel)` helper (or an `emitDomainEvent(bus, event, payload)` helper) that:
- Runs the state-persisting workflow first.
- Only after success, emits the domain event in its own try/catch with a distinct log line ("failed to emit X — workflow succeeded").
- Collapses the duplicated per-row try/catch + logging boilerplate across all three subscribers.

Also collapses the related Minor finding on duplicated boilerplate across the three subscribers.

## Individual sub-issues

One sub-task per subscriber file to migrate to the shared helper.

title: P1: Tighten "any" type holes at every module boundary (Ongoing REST / query.graph / container.resolve)
description:
Cross-shard epic from whole-project Medusa-aware code review 2026-07-02 (P1). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## Pattern

The `any` type-hole shortcut was adopted consistently across every module boundary. Its cost surfaces as three independent type holes today and a compile-clean landmine for every future refactor.

## Instances

- `src/lib/ongoing/client.ts:155` — `mapInventoryRow(raw: any)` (I1)
- `src/lib/ongoing/client.ts:170` — `mapTrackedOrder(raw: any)` (I2)
- `src/lib/ongoing/re-query-fulfillment-order.ts:34` — `query: any` (I3)
- `src/workflows/steps/create-ongoing-integration-row.ts:40` — `input as any` (I6, hides unique-constraint MedusaError)
- `src/workflows/steps/update-ongoing-integration.ts:56, 79` — `input as any` on update + compensation (I7)
- Plus **45+ instances** of `container: any` / `service: any` across `src/workflows/steps/*.ts` (Shard-3 finding S3-M-any).
- Plus `eventBus as any` in the 3 subscribers and 2 jobs (Shard-5 finding).

## Failure modes

- Fields that Ongoing omits at runtime (e.g. `article` on inventory rows) flow into required fields silently — downstream code that keys off them operates on `undefined` and drops/mis-attributes state (I1, I2).
- Renaming a method or field on the module service is compile-clean everywhere the resolved value is `any` — bugs only surface at runtime as "not a function" or silent dropped writes.
- DB-level unique-constraint violations aren't translated to MedusaError types → API returns opaque 500 instead of 409 (I6).

## Recommended approach

- Introduce runtime validation at the Ongoing edge (Zod / valibot / io-ts) so `raw: any` becomes a typed schema at the boundary of `client.ts`.
- Generate types for `container.resolve(ONGOING_MODULE)` from the module service signatures, or type the resolve call site explicitly (`resolve<OngoingModuleService>(ONGOING_MODULE)`).
- Type the resolve of `Modules.EVENT_BUS` with a narrow local interface (as done selectively elsewhere in the codebase).
- Do this as one epic so the boundary types are consistent across the codebase, not in per-file drips.

## Individual sub-issues

Break this epic into sub-tasks per boundary once the approach is decided (client → module → step → subscriber). Track under this issue via the native sub-issue relationship.

title: Add compare-and-swap on retry_count in retry-failed-syncs.ts to avoid double-increment under multi-instance overlap (residual from CRIT-7)
description:
Residual from review CRIT-7 refutation (2026-07-02). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## File
`src/jobs/retry-failed-syncs.ts:156-193`

## Context

The whole-project review flagged retry-failed-syncs.ts for missing `acquireSyncLock`/`releaseSyncLock` versus its sibling jobs `status-poll.ts` and `stock-sync.ts` (CRIT-7 original claim). Adversarial refute confirmed the "duplicate Ongoing order push" consequence doesn't hold — `pushOrderRecordSyncStep` calls `client.putOrder(model)` which is explicitly an idempotent upsert keyed by `ongoing_order_number`. The plan doc for #39 self-documents this choice.

**But the refuter surfaced a narrower residual:** two overlapping ticks (multi-instance deployment, or a slow tick still running past the next minute boundary) can both pass the `isRetryDue` check and both increment `retry_count`. There's no compare-and-swap. Result: double-increment of the retry counter and double Ongoing API calls for that row.

## Failure scenario

Two `retry-failed-syncs` job instances run on overlapping ticks. Both list the same due row (`sync_state: 'error'`, `error_class: 'retryable'`, `next_retry_at < now`). Both invoke `pushOrderToOngoing`. The Ongoing PUT is idempotent so no duplicate order is created — but `retry_count` is incremented twice via `service.updateOrderSync({retry_count: current + 1})` in a plain last-write-wins pattern. Backoff computations for the next retry are now wrong (potentially skips a due window or halves the interval).

Not data corruption. But it distorts backoff and doubles Ongoing rate-limit consumption for that row.

## Recommended fix

- Add a compare-and-swap on `retry_count` (`WHERE retry_count = expected AND sync_state = 'error'`), or
- Add a per-row lock scoped to the due-window processing (analogous to `acquireSyncLock` but keyed per-row instead of per-integration).

The plan for #39 explicitly opted out of the sibling-job lock; this narrower fix targets the actual leftover race.

title: Narrow terminal-error swallow in cancelOngoingOrderStep to specific 'already cancelled' shape (residual from CRIT-3)
description:
Residual from review CRIT-3 refutation (2026-07-02). See `scratchpad/medusa-review-report.md`.

## File
`src/workflows/steps/cancel-ongoing-order.ts:29-36`

## Context

The whole-project review flagged the client-level DELETE retry as mis-classifying "already cancelled" as terminal (CRIT-3 original claim). Adversarial refute found that the step already catches `err instanceof OngoingApiError && err.kind === 'terminal'` and returns `StepResponse({cancelled:false, swallowed:true})` — idempotent-success handler. **But the refuter surfaced a narrower residual:** the swallow keys on `kind === 'terminal'` (any 4xx), not on the specific "already cancelled" message match. A genuinely-different 400 error (malformed order id, permissions issue, contract violation) is silently swallowed as a false success too.

## Failure scenario

Ongoing returns 400 with a `not-yet-implemented feature` / `unauthorized order id format` error (not "already cancelled"). The step catches it as `kind: 'terminal'` and returns `{cancelled: false, swallowed: true}` as a success. The workflow proceeds to `markOrderSyncCancelledStep` and writes an incorrect terminal state — the merchant's cancel appears successful, but no cancellation actually happened at Ongoing.

Narrow the swallow to match the specific Ongoing error shape/message for "already cancelled" only. All other terminal 4xx should re-throw or classify as a real failure so the retry-failed-syncs workflow can surface them.

title: Retry driver must cap on OngoingOrderSync.retry_count (dead-letter deterministic failures)
description:
Forward note from the #67/#73 review. #67 made unknown/network errors classify as `retryable` (correct — avoids dead-lettering on transient outages). Consequence: once a **retry driver** is built (re-runs sync rows with `error_class = "retryable"`), a *deterministic* non-network failure (a programming bug, or malformed-but-non-`OngoingApiError` data) would be retried forever instead of dead-lettering.

The `OngoingOrderSync` model already has a `retry_count` column (default 0), so the design anticipates a cap. **Requirement for the retry driver:** honor `retry_count` as a max-attempts ceiling — after N attempts, stop retrying and mark the row terminal/dead-lettered.

No consumer exists yet (no retry driver in M2). Tracking so it isn't lost when the retry mechanism lands. Related: #67.

title: Classify unknown/network errors as retryable in Ongoing sync (not terminal)
description:
Surfaced in the #26 Medusa review. In `pushOrderRecordSyncHandler` (and the client retry loop), errors are classified via `err instanceof OngoingApiError ? err.kind : undefined`, so a raw network error (ECONNRESET / timeout / DNS / a `fetch` TypeError) yields `undefined` → `error_class = "terminal"`. The client `request()` retry loop also only retries `OngoingApiError` with `kind: "retryable"`. Net effect: a brief outage permanently flags the sync row `terminal` and requires manual intervention.

This matched the plan's explicit decision and was non-blocking for #26 because the retry consumer (#21) isn't built yet. Fix before #21 relies on it: classify unknown/non-API/network errors as `retryable` (or detect transient network failures explicitly) so they get retried rather than dead-lettered.

Surfaced during M2 Wave 2 (#23). Follow-up to #52.

title: Clear edit-blocked state on successful re-sync (banner goes stale otherwise)
description:
## Context

Surfaced by the M5 cross-plan review of #93 (widget banner) + #94 (order-updated post-workflow persist).

Both #93 and #94 correctly scoped out **clear-on-success** — nulling the `edit_blocked_*` fields on `OngoingOrderSync` when a later re-sync succeeds. It was #91's explicitly-optional Task 6 and was not implemented for either subscriber.

**Consequence:** once a row is marked edit-blocked, a subsequent successful re-sync never nulls `edit_blocked_at` / `edit_blocked_category` / `edit_blocked_reason`. So the order-widget "Edit blocked" banner (#93) becomes **permanently sticky** in production — it will keep showing even after the edit successfully re-syncs.

## Proposed fix

On the success path of each edit re-sync (the `if (result?.synced)` branches in `src/subscribers/order-updated.ts` and `src/subscribers/order-edit-confirmed.ts`), call `markOrderSyncEditBlockedWorkflow(container).run({ input: { order_sync_id: row.id, blocked: false } })` to null the three fields (the workflow/step already support `blocked: false` per #91).

## Relates to

- #91 (persisted the fields + wired the workflow; clear-on-success was its optional Task 6)
- #93 (renders the banner that would go stale)
- #94 (adds the order-updated post-workflow persist site)

title: pre-push hook blocks all non-fast-forward pushes, forcing branch delete+recreate on rebase
description:
## Problem

`scripts/pre-push` rejects **any** non-fast-forward push, with no exception for rebasing your own feature branch. When an open PR's branch is rebased onto an advanced `main` (a normal way to resolve merge conflicts), `git push --force-with-lease` is rejected by the hook.

## Impact

During M5 wave-1, PR #96 (issue #44) needed a rebase after sibling PR #95 (#91) merged and touched the same subscriber files. The force-push was blocked, so the branch had to be **deleted and recreated** (which the hook permits — it skips the ancestor check when the remote ref is freshly created). GitHub then auto-closes a PR whose head branch is deleted and refuses to reopen one whose branch was recreated, so a **new PR (#99)** had to be opened to replace #96. This adds churn (lost PR history/discussion, new number) every time a PR needs a post-review rebase.

## Suggested fix

Scope the non-fast-forward block to **protected branches only** (e.g. `main`), and allow force-with-lease on feature branches. Alternatively, document the delete+recreate (and resulting new-PR) workaround in the process docs so it's a known, deliberate step rather than a surprise.

## Discovered by

M5 parallel wave execution (`/work-milestone`); surfaced when rebasing #96 → became #99. See also the `npx tsc` fake-success and RTK `git diff` compaction findings from the same run (separate concerns).

title: order-updated.ts: persist edit-blocked state when workflow's internal re-gate blocks (post-workflow site)
description:
## Context

Surfaced during code review of #91 (persist edit-blocked state on `OngoingOrderSync`).

`src/subscribers/order-edit-confirmed.ts` has **two** blocked-emit sites and #91 wires `markOrderSyncEditBlockedWorkflow` at both: the pre-check (`!allowed`) and the post-workflow site where `syncOrderEditToOngoing` itself returns `result.blocked === true` (a race where status changes between the subscriber's own query and the workflow's internal re-gate).

`src/subscribers/order-updated.ts` only ever had **one** blocked-emit site (the pre-check) before #91 — it never emitted `ongoing.sync.edit_blocked` at a post-workflow site, so #91 (which only wires *existing* emit sites) did not add persistence there either. Its post-workflow branch today is:

```ts
if (result?.synced) {
  logger.info(...)
} else {
  logger.warn(`... re-sync not applied ... (workflow: ${result?.reason ?? "unknown"})`)
  // no event emitted, no field write
}
```

`syncOrderEditToOngoing`'s result shape (`src/workflows/sync-order-edit-to-ongoing.ts:6-27`) already carries `{ synced, blocked, reason }`, so the data needed to detect and persist this case is available — it's just unused today.

## Proposed fix

Mirror `order-edit-confirmed.ts`'s post-workflow branch in `order-updated.ts`:
- When `result?.blocked` is true (or `!result?.synced`), emit `ongoing.sync.edit_blocked` (currently not emitted at all at this site — a separate, smaller gap) and call `markOrderSyncEditBlockedWorkflow(container).run({ input: { order_sync_id: row.id, blocked: true, category: "address_contact", reason: result?.reason ?? "status_blocked" } })`.

## Not in scope

Do not fold this into #91 — that PR intentionally scoped itself to wiring only the pre-existing emit sites literally in the issue text, to minimize merge-conflict surface with concurrent #42/#44 subscriber-file work.

title: Persist edit-blocked state on OngoingOrderSync (model field + migration + subscriber write)
description:

title: Validate defaultStatusPollInterval (NaN guard) in status-poll job
description:
Surfaced by the independent Medusa review of PR #85 (issue #34).

`OngoingModuleService.getDefaultStatusPollIntervalMs()` does `parseInt(this.options_.defaultStatusPollInterval ?? "60000", 10)` with **no finite/>0 guard**, and `resolveIntervalMs` in `src/jobs/status-poll.ts` only validates the *per-integration* `status_poll_interval`, falling through to the default unchecked.

**Failure:** a misconfigured non-numeric `defaultStatusPollInterval` plugin option yields `NaN` → `isDue` (`now - last >= NaN`) is always false, so an integration polls **once then never again**, and `acquireSyncLock` stamps `new Date(now + NaN)` = `Invalid Date`. Silent (no error), config-time only.

**Fix:** apply the same `Number.isFinite(parsed) && parsed > 0` guard to the default branch (fall back to 60000), and/or validate `defaultStatusPollInterval` in `src/modules/ongoing/options.ts`.

Source: PR #85 / #34.

title: Webhook route: wrap post-auth handler body in try/catch to avoid 500 on transient errors
description:
Surfaced by the independent Medusa review of PR #80 (issue #35).

In `src/api/ongoing/webhooks/[credentialKey]/route.ts`, the **post-authentication** path (`req.scope.resolve(ONGOING_MODULE)`, `await listOngoingIntegrations(...)`, and the `shipped_status_codes as number[]` access on a `model.json().nullable()` column) is not wrapped — a DB/config error throws and surfaces as a **500**.

This is **only reachable after a valid X-Auth-Token**, so it is *not* an unauthenticated enumeration vector (the uniform-401 surface is intact). At worst a verified Ongoing delivery gets a 500 and is retried by Ongoing's retry policy.

**Recommendation:** wrap the post-auth body in try/catch and return a retry-friendly acknowledgement (consistent with the always-200, downstream-idempotent contract), logging the error server-side.

Likely best addressed alongside #36 (which fills the dispatch seam in this same handler's in-band branch). Source: PR #80 / #35; relates to #36.

title: Harden syncOngoingShipment idempotency against Medusa error-string coupling
description:
Surfaced by the independent Medusa review of PR #82 (issue #33).

`applyOrderShipmentStep` treats an already-shipped fulfillment as idempotent success by matching the **exact message string** `MedusaError(NOT_ALLOWED, "Shipment has already been created")` thrown by Medusa core-flow's `validate-shipment` step. Verified correct against pinned Medusa **2.16.0**.

**Risk:** a future Medusa version that rewords that message would silently flip the already-shipped case from *idempotent no-op* into a *recorded terminal error* on `OngoingOrderSync` — a regression with no compile-time or test signal (unit tests mock the core-flow).

**Options (low priority, defensive):**
- Add a comment pinning the assumption to the Medusa version, and/or
- Match on `err.type === MedusaError.Types.NOT_ALLOWED` plus a narrower signal instead of the full message, and/or
- Add an integration test against the real `createOrderShipmentWorkflow` that re-asserts the swallow contract, to fail loudly on a Medusa bump.

Source: PR #82 / #33. Not a current defect (2.16.0 is pinned).

title: gate-order-edit collapses to first row when medusa_fulfillment_id is null (multi-row mis-targeting)
description:
Flagged independently by the Medusa reviews of #31 (PR #71) and #54 (PR #70).

**Root cause:** `src/workflows/steps/gate-order-edit.ts` — when `medusa_fulfillment_id` is null/absent, the gate falls back to `list({ medusa_order_id })[0]` (first row only). For an order with ≥2 `OngoingOrderSync` rows that all have null `medusa_fulfillment_id`, every per-row iteration in the order-edit / order.updated subscribers re-resolves to the *same first row*, so rows 2..N are mis-targeted.

**Reachability:** Low in M2 — `latest_status_code` defaults to null so the gate stays closed until status polling lands, and in practice each sync row carries a `medusa_fulfillment_id` from its pushed fulfillment. Becomes reachable once status polling populates `latest_status_code` AND a null-fulfillment multi-row order occurs.

**Fix:** target the gate by the sync row's own id (`order_sync_id` — the subscribers already have `row.id`) instead of collapsing to the first row by `medusa_order_id`.

Pre-existing contract gap in #27's gate step (not introduced by #31/#54). Consumers: #31, #54. Placed in M3 since it's only reachable once status polling exists.

title: Defensive: keep stock-sync delta cursor < Ongoing's 24h stockInfoChangedFrom limit
description: Ongoing rejects stockInfoChangedFrom older than 24h with HTTP 400 ('must be within 24 hours of the current time'), confirmed live. Today the stock-sync job is safe: FULL_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS=6h forces a full sweep (changed_since=null) well before the delta cursor could age past 24h. This is an IMPLICIT coupling — if FULL_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS is ever raised >=24h, delta ticks would start 400ing. Consider clamping changed_since to now-24h (or falling back to a full sweep) in the delta path, and/or an assertion that FULL_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS < 24h. Non-blocking; found while building the live harness (9sp).
